newsitem.title: USA: Simpson compensatory award tops similar cases.
newsitem.headline: Simpson compensatory award tops similar cases.

text.p: By Gail Appleson, U.S. Law Correspondent

The $8.5 million compensatory damage award against O.J. Simpson for the wrongful death of Ronald Goldman exceeds the largest such award for male victims of Goldman's age, jury researchers said on Thursday.

Jury Verdict Research, based in Horsham, Pennsylvania, said its 112,000-case database of personal injury verdicts and settlements showed compensatory awards for the wrongful death of men aged 25-29 ranged from $4,654 to $8 million from 1989 through 1996. The average award was $1.06 million and the median was $633,000.
The company said awards of $1 million or more made up 38 percent of those verdict amounts.

Goldman was 25 years old when he and Nicole Brown Simpson, 35, were stabbed to death on June 12, 1994. A California jury on Tuesday blamed the former football star for their deaths and ordered him to pay $8.5 million in compensatory damages to Goldman's family for the loss of his love, companionship and moral support.
Simpson was acquitted on criminal charges in 1995.

Russell Moran, publisher of The New York Jury Verdict Reporter, said he felt the compensatory award carried a punitive element. "I would view it to be excessive," he said. "The jury expressed an opinion with that award."

The jury must now decide on punitive damages and Daniel Petrocelli, the plaintiffs' lead attorney, urged panellists on Thursday to punish Simpson with heavy damages. Jurors are to base their decision on how reprehensible the crime was and how much the award would hurt Simpson financially.

Jury Verdict Research found that in California, punitive damage awards for the wrongful death of men 18 and over ranged from $5,000 to $3 million from 1989 to 1996. The average punitive award was $678,250.
California juries awarded punitive damages for the wrongful death of women 18 and over that ranged from $20,000 to $7.75 million. The average was $2.63 million.
Nationally, the punitive verdict range for men aged 25-29 was $800 to $25 million. The national average was $3.17 million.
For the wrongful death of women 30-39, which would include females of Nicole Brown Simpson's age, the national punitive verdict range was $20,000 to $45 million. The average award was $7.13 million.
